title: Consolidate idempotency, hedging, and circuit-breaker policies across services and SDKs
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: We need a single, operationally-safe contract for retries, timeouts, backoff, idempotency keys, hedged requests, and circuit-breaker/load-shed behavior across the platform and official SDKs. Current service-level ad-hoc implementations cause inconsistent client behavior, difficult incident investigations, and uneven SLO burn. This ticket defines the contract, implements runtime and SDK changes, and rolls out a migration with feature flags and monitoring to keep regressions <1% error-budget impact.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical spec published and approved by SRE/Runtime/SDK teams (confluence link in comments)
Runtime implements server-side idempotency dedupe with configured TTL and metrics exposure
Official JS/Python SDKs provide idempotency helpers and opt-in automatic hedging toggle
Circuit-breaker library consolidated and exposed via service config; default thresholds documented
Load-shedding policy implemented that maps to customer tier and returns structured 429 with Retry-After and reason
Migration plan executed behind feature flags: canary -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with rollback playbook
Dashboards and alerts added: per-route p99/p95 latency, error-rate, hedged-request-rate, idempotency-collisions, and SLO burn rate
notes: Design goal: developer-visible defaults that are safe for most workloads but tunable per-route/customer
Prefer server-side dedupe for idempotency; SDK helpers only generate keys and attach headers
Hedging is opt-in at SDK and runtime level; runtime can auto-enable for routes that exceed SLO-driven latency patterns
Circuit-breaker decisions combine error-rate and sustained latency signals to avoid tripping on transient spikes
Load-shedding hierarchy: reserved capacity -> paid tier -> best-effort -> degraded-model fallback
Non-goal: full client-side request replay of non-idempotent mutations (we will document and mark these as non-retryable)
We will keep a compact compatibility layer for older SDK versions during migration window
implementation_plan: Week 0: Publish spec and compatibility matrix; gather approvers from SRE, runtime, SDK, PM
Week 1: Implement server-side idempotency store with TTL 24h and idempotency header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key
Week 2: Integrate circuit-breaker library with thresholds: open when error_ratio > 0.05 over 30s OR p99 latency > 3x SLO for 1 minute
Week 3: Add load-shedding token buckets per tier and 429 schema (x-redwood-retry-after, x-redwood-shed-reason)
Week 4: SDK updates: idempotency helper, default retry/backoff config (exp backoff base=100ms cap=2000ms, max_retries=3), and AutomaticHedging config
Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with monitoring and rollback triggers documented in runbook
risk_and_tradeoffs: Server-side dedupe increases memory/kv usage; we mitigate with TTL and bloom-filter-style pre-checks for high-volume routes
Aggressive hedging reduces latency but increases GPU/throughput cost; hedging defaults are conservative and require opt-in for high-volume routes
Tight circuit-breakers protect SLOs but may cause customer-visible throttling; thresholds tuned per-traffic-profile to minimize false opens
Backwards compatibility: older SDKs remain supported but will not receive hedging/auto-idempotency helpers until upgraded
observability_requirements: Metrics: idempotency_hits, idempotency_collisions, hedged_request_rate, hedged_success_rate, cb_state_by_route, shed_count_by_tier
Dashboards: per-route SLO mapping with p50/p95/p99 latency and error budget burn
Alerts: sustained SLO burn > 5% per 10m, hedged_success_rate < 50% on canary, idempotency_collision_rate > 0.1%
Logs: structured 429 responses include shed reason and originating route; correlate request_id and idempotency_key
rollout_playbook: Create feature flag (reliability.consolidated-retries) scoped by service and region
Canary in us-west-2 at 2% traffic for 24h; validate dashboards and no increased error budget burn
Progress to 25% for 48h, then 75% for 24h, then 100% if no regressions
Rollback: disable flag and run /runbooks/reliability/retry-backoff-rollback.md; notify customers impacted via status page
Post-mortem: require RC <72h if rollforward causes >1% SLO regression
